text:
meera_netops: FLAGGING - Customer RED-789 reporting intermittent failures to their Private API endpoint after we applied peering change in region-us-west-2. Symptoms: TLS handshake errors from some subnets, other subnets fine. CX opened SUP-14209. Anyone on call?

josh_sre: on it. first question: is this IPsec or Direct Connect/DX?

meera_netops: they are on a Direct Connect hosted connection with BGP peering to our VPC router. We did a small config push to route filters ~20m ago.

alan_support: seeing SUP-14209 notes: "tls: remote error: handshake failure" for 3 of 8 customer AZs. Customer says routes sometimes drop and come back.

kim_network: grabbing BGP status from our edge. run:
```
show ip bgp summary vrf redwood-priv
Neighbor        V    AS MsgRcv MsgSent   TblVer  InQ OutQ Up/Down  State/PfxRcd
10.24.5.2       4 65001   1243   1240  1234567    0    0 01:12:34  1200
10.24.6.2       4 65123     12    150  1234567    0    0 00:00:12  Idle (ASN mismatch)
```

kim_network: note neighbor .6.2 shows Idle with "ASN mismatch". our expected customer ASN is 65123 per onboarding, but the established neighbor .5.2 is 65001.

meera_netops: customer config snap shows they recently changed their edge ASN accidentally to 65001 in one of their routers during a maintenance window. That would explain asymmetric route advertisements.

alan_support: that fits. some AZs prefer the broken peer and get no routes -> TLS handshake fails because traffic takes the wrong path or NAT.

customer_ops: confirming — we rolled back a script but one router didn't pick up the correct ASN. We can correct on our side if needed.

infra-bot: [deploy] route-filter-update applied to vrf redwood-priv by kim_network (id: cfg-9912)

josh_sre: proposed immediate steps: 1) coordinate with customer to set ASN to 65123 on the misconfigured router 2) clear BGP session on their side OR run 'clear bgp neighbor 10.24.6.2' from our router 3) monitor prefix table and TLS handshakes 4) collect tcpdump if still failing.

meera_netops: please also check route-maps for as-path prepends that might push traffic different places.

customer_ops: making change now to set ASN 65123 on router rtr-east-2, will message when done.

(12:03) customer_ops: changed ASN to 65123 and restarted BGP on rtr-east-2.

kim_network: re-checking BGP summary: 
```
show ip bgp summary vrf redwood-priv
Neighbor        V    AS MsgRcv MsgSent   TblVer  InQ OutQ Up/Down  State/PfxRcd
10.24.5.2       4 65001   1243   1240  1234567    0    0 01:15:12  1200
10.24.6.2       4 65123  1532   1528  1234571    0    0 00:02:34  1198
```

kim_network: good — both neighbors are ESTABLISHED now and advertising prefixes. Slight difference in pfx count due to filter order but both show ~1198-1200 routes.

josh_sre: run a quick tcpdump on our edge to validate TLS handshake success from affected subnet 10.50.12.0/24:
```
sudo tcpdump -ni eth1 host 10.50.12.45 and port 443 -w /tmp/redwood-sup14209.pcap
```

meera_netops: customer confirmed TLS now succeeds from previously failing AZ. Monitoring for 10 minutes.

alan_support: collecting logs from our gateway:
```
2026-03-17T12:08:33Z gateway[tls]: conn from 10.50.12.45: source verified, handshake complete
2026-03-17T12:08:34Z proxy: request forwarded to private endpoint 10.100.8.12
```

customer_ops: all checks green on our side too. SUP-14209 -> marking resolved from CX perspective.

josh_sre: postmortem notes to include: root cause = customer-side router misconfigured ASN on single BGP peer after maintenance. Contributing factor = our recent route-filter change made one peer's idle state cause asymmetric routing faster than expected.

meera_netops: action items: 1) update onboarding checklist to verify BGP ASN on all customer routers before peering goes live (owner: network-onboarding) 2) add automated alert when BGP neighbor state == Idle (ASN mismatch) for >30s (owner: eng-infra monitoring) 3) document tcpdump and 'show ip bgp summary' quick checks in runbook (owner: support)

alex_dedicated: also adding a small guardrail: when deploying route-filter updates that change acceptance lists, run a preflight that checks neighbor ASNs and flags mismatches.

sre-bot: created ticket INFRA-5643 for monitoring alert and ONBOARD-89 for onboarding checklist update.

meera_netops: thanks everyone. closing thread, will attach SUP-14209 link and PCAP to ticket INFRA-5643 for retention. :thumbsup:

alan_support: follow-up: please confirm once runbook is updated so we can close SUP-14209 fully with CX.

meera_netops: will post updates in #eng-infra when done.

(12:20) end of thread."
